claim: Error feedback is what makes proof repair work: a repair model given the failed proof plus the checker error beats resampling at equal cost; the same model without the error text does not.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: resample N vs revise-with-checker-error vs revise-without-error on a formal or executable task.

claim: The cost-matched gain of one repair over resampling is small (Baldur: +1.5 points abstract, second repair only +0.8 over plain generation at cost 3). Gap-search update: Olausson 2024 (GPT-4 APPS 1.05x with 10 drafts + 1 repair, 0.97x with 2 drafts + 10 repairs) and Lean step-level repair (+2.3 to +4.1 points over sampling at matched wall-clock) agree that gains are modest and depend on spending budget on first drafts.
agent_test: Count repair rounds at equal tokens; cap at 1-2 rounds.

claim: Repair gain grows with a stronger external checker: Goedel-V2 correction gives about +2 points on miniF2F pass@32 and +14 solves on PutnamBench; 5 rounds with 128k context reaches 92.7% at pass@32, above 92.2% for pass@8192 without correction.
agent_test: Compare k-round compiler-feedback revision against pass@k at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0); oracle labels explain earlier gains. Gap-search update: Kamoi 2024 survey finds no success with feedback from prompted LLMs outside tasks suited to it; Self-Debug drops without execution (MBPP Codex 61.4 to 57.6); CRITIC without tools is flat or worse. Reasoning-era models are not tested by these sources.
agent_test: Equal-token: revise-without-verifier vs resample; revise only when a verifier flags failure. Note b20 and c16 and c27 are the same paper, so counted as one source; consistent with the Baldur no-error-message arm.

claim: Backtracking is the dominant component of a repair loop: PALM without backtracking falls from 40.4% to 6.5%, while removing any one repair rule costs only 1.6-2.6 points.
agent_test: Ablate backtracking vs local repair rules in the agent's revise step.

claim: Symbolic/tool repair is complementary to LLM regeneration: Tool Correction (Lyra), CoqHammer fallback (PALM, Cobblestone) and Sledgehammer union (Baldur+Thor 65.7% vs Thor 57.0%) each add large gains.
agent_test: Arm with a strong deterministic tool as fallback vs LLM-only at equal tokens.

claim: Keeping verified parts of a failed proof and re-prompting only for failing subgoals is more token efficient than regenerating from scratch (Cobblestone 59.3K vs 99.3K tokens per theorem; APOLLO 362 vs 25,600 samples for similar accuracy).
agent_test: Compare partial-repair (keep passing steps) with full regeneration at equal tokens.

claim: Localised repair at matched sample budget gives modest not huge gains: APOLLO +0.9 on Goedel-V2-8B, +4.2 on Kimina-7B; large jumps (o3-mini 3.3 to 40.2) come from fixing format/syntax failures.
agent_test: Check what share of repair gain is syntax/format fixing; run a repair arm after a format fixer.

claim: Plan-then-fill (informal draft, formal sketch with gaps, tool fills gaps) beats direct proof: miniF2F-test 20.9 to 39.3 (DSP); removing the prover costs 9.0 points. Gap-search update: LAMP without its Planner loses 11.1 points (96.7 to 85.6, Hard 88.2 to 58.8); P3 joint program-and-proof planning beats program-then-proof by +4.6 to +11.2 points on four frontier backends.
agent_test: Sketch-with-holes arm vs direct arm at equal tokens.

claim: Plan quality matters but not monotonically: human informal proofs gave 51.2% vs GPT-4 informal 47.9% on test (Lyra), yet in DSP a larger Minerva (540B) gave a worse test score than 8B (30.3 vs 36.5).
agent_test: Vary plan quality independent of fill model; check for plan-model-size interactions.

claim: Conjecture Correction (regenerating the sketch from error) adds little by itself (+0.4) and helps only when a strong tool fills gaps (+5.3 with Tool Correction).
agent_test: Test plan-level revision vs step-level revision.

claim: Tree search with truncate-and-resume gives only a small gain over naive retry: RMaxTS 62.7 vs 60.2 single pass; ProofAug reports under 0.2% advantage over naive retrying at 3200 samples.
agent_test: Compare naive retry vs structured search at equal tokens.

claim: Hierarchical planner-plus-prover decomposition gives the largest reported results: Hilbert 99.2% miniF2F, 70.0% PutnamBench; the planner matters more than the prover (Gemini Pro beats Flash by 3-4 points).
agent_test: Planner strength vs executor strength ablation at equal tokens. Caveat: results are not token-matched to baselines.

claim: Retrieval of similar earlier proofs from the same project raises success (Rango +47% theorems; Baldur theory-file context 40.7 to 47.5).
agent_test: Retrieval of own earlier solved cases vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Error taxonomy of LLM proof attempts: most errors are low-level (wrong theorem application 49.6%, invalid reference 15.2%), high-level structure is usually right. Gap-search update: in the Lean step-level repair study one repair recovered only 6.2% of 89,634 rejected tactics; recovery is 11-15% for no-progress, apply/exact and rfl failures and about 2% for type mismatch and syntax.
agent_test: Classify the agent's own failures before choosing repair type.

claim: Failure analysis: missing premises dominate residual PALM failures (58 of 100 premises not retrieved).
agent_test: Check whether repair failures come from missing knowledge rather than reasoning.

claim: The founding Edinburgh claim (critics: failure of a method triggers lemma/generalisation patch) is a design argument backed by worked examples, with no head-to-head success counts against other provers in the text read.
agent_test: Treat as design inspiration; test failure-pattern-to-patch mapping directly.

claim: Proof repair has a built-in specification to check patches, avoiding program-repair overfitting; symbolic repair across type changes works for structured changes (Pumpkin Pi) but saved no time for added constructors.
agent_test: Always check repaired output against the original statement.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Repeated repair has diminishing returns: gains shrink with rounds (APOLLO r=0..6: 57.6, 60.7, 63.5, 65.6; Baldur second repair +1.3). Gap-search update: in Lean step-level repair the first repair gives 84 to 96% of the total gain and marginal efficiency falls over fifteen-fold after round 1; Self-Debug: one turn is typically enough (later turns within 0.1%).
agent_test: Set a round cap and measure the marginal gain per round.

claim: Lean proof-repair evidence is mostly on benchmarks with possible training-data contamination; only Cobblestone explicitly controls for leakage.
agent_test: Use fresh or private problems for agent tests.

claim: Diagnosis, not rewriting, is the bottleneck of repair: replacing GPT-4's own feedback with expert human feedback raises repair success 33.3% to 52.6% (1.58x); a stronger feedback model lifts weaker coders above both resampling and self-repair; a known mistake location lets models fix chain-of-thought traces they cannot locate themselves.
agent_test: Arms at equal tokens: generic self-review vs pointed critique from a checker or stronger model vs oracle location; measure repair rate.

claim: Local patching works mainly on shallow failures: structural errors (type mismatch, strategy errors) are rarely fixed by a patch, so a repair operator needs an error-type router that sends structural failures to re-planning.
agent_test: Tag failures as local or structural; compare patch vs re-plan success per tag at equal tokens.

claim: Repair loops drift the goal: LLM repair that passes the checker sometimes edits what it should not (CAPRI: 6 of 144 accepted candidates, 8.7% in iterative full-theory workflows; a drifted development had 16 of 100 declarations materially changed, one theorem weakened). Restricting edits to the proof body gave 0 violations at 29/36 vs 31/36.
agent_test: After each revision, diff the claim being answered against the original question and fail the revision on any change.

claim: Iterating on real prover output beats one shot in Isabelle repair (22/36 vs 31-32/36, paired p=0.03) but showing the diagnostic in the first request does not help much (24/36 vs 22/36).
agent_test: Compare one shot, one shot with error, and iterate-after-failure at matched tokens.

claim: Most failures are not plan errors: in P3 failures on Verina only 4 of 48 were blamed on an inadequate plan (15 on proof elaboration, 26 timeout or tool fault), and 92.9% of successes kept the first plan; plan-level revision has a small target.
agent_test: Log failure cause per run; only add plan-rewrite if plan errors are a large share.
